config.design: F arm = e1's 4 attn_every seeds at 0.2b (free control); W arm = web_hq_step01/ x 4 seeds; MDE = 1.98 x measured sigma
config.kill_rule: Step 0/1 hit rate on web_hq < 2% -> no contrast (arms 98%+ identical; effect bound p x delta_marginal < 0.02 nat < MDE); rule written BEFORE seeing the number
config.verdict: killed by its own pre-registered threshold, NOT a null result: the experiment had no contrast to measure; the rule for saying so was set in advance. The surviving finding: the knife is already in the corpus — the old garbage chain cleaned web_hq at build time (pre-df2b774 chain hits 0/50000, confirming 3b's PROVENANCE record), so Step 0/1's marginal capture is 0.33%. Any filter upgrade on this corpus now has a number to beat.
config.successor: weight ablation 32.4%->20% approved as a SEPARATE independent experiment (different question, different reading rules); queues behind the six ladder points; sizing waits on sigma_hat from e1's 0.2b seeds; design to fb before GPU allocation
config.precision_read: 100-doc human read (3b) was conditional on p>=2% — cancelled with the experiment
config.outcome: killed_by_threshold -- the experiment was declared unmeasurable by a rule written before the number existed, not refuted and not null. A null says we looked and saw nothing; this says two arms 99.67% identical have no contrast to measure. Kept in config rather than status: the schema's four statuses describe a fact's evidential standing, not an experiment's fate, and adding a fifth would make every consumer learn a value only this entry uses.
